question: Severe ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) — characterised by haemoconcentration, oliguria, and ascites — can usually be managed safely with outpatient observation and increased fluid intake alone.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Severe OHSS (haemoconcentration, oliguria, ascites, respiratory distress) mandates hospital admission. Complications include deep vein thrombosis, ARDS, and acute renal failure — these cannot be safely monitored in the outpatient setting.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Severe OHSS requires hospital admission. It carries risks of thromboembolism, renal failure, and ARDS. Management includes IV fluid replacement (albumin if needed), thromboprophylaxis, and in some cases paracentesis. Outpatient management is appropriate only for mild-moderate OHSS.
